newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks update on China's top dissident.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks update on China's top dissident.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it was pressing China for information about its best-known dissident, reportedly being imprisoned in worsening conditions.
"We are gravely concerned and we are seeking additional information" about dissident Wei Jingsheng, who is serving a 14-year term for subversion, State Department spokesman John Dinger said.

Prison authorities have accused Wei, often described as the father of China's struggling democracy movement, of brawling with another inmate and have imposed new punishments, a family member who visited him in mid-June said.
Electricity to Wei's cell has been cut off and he has been banned from shopping at the prison canteen, said the relative, who expressed concern about Wei's health.
"We again call on China to release Wei and all others who have been imprisoned or detained for the peaceful expression of their political and religious views," Dinger said.

He said the United States had asked both the Chinese Embassy in Washington and authorities in Beijing for an update on Wei, who is imprisoned at the Nanpu salt farm, a labour camp in the northern province of Hebei.
Wei, 47, blames the deterioration of his prison conditions on what he considers Western reluctance to criticise China's human rights policies, a relative told Reuters in Beijing.

Dinger, asked to comment on the charge, said no other country had been more openly and persistently critical of China's human rights record than the United States. "I think our record on that speaks for itself," he said.
